1.explanation: All of the missing highlighting constructs live in the bash.js language definition.  The top-level export function builds and returns the Bash grammar but currently only includes modes for comments, quotes, variables, arithmetic expansions, functions and shebangs.  Pipes (|), I/O redirections (<, >), heredoc/here-string markers (<<, <<<), and the line-continuation backslash are never declared as separate modes, so hljs never assigns them a token class.  To fix the issue you must modify the export default function to add operator patterns (for |, <, >), a continuation rule for trailing backslashes, and a heredoc here-doc/here-string matcher alongside the existing SUBST/VAR rules so those punctuation elements become highlighted.
1.bug_scenario: In the screenshots the user’s Bash snippets still show plain text for pipeline (|), redirection operators (<, >), here-doc markers (<<, <<<) and the line-continuation backslash (\) — none of these are picked up by the existing bash highlighter.  Likewise, while $(…) substitution is partially implemented, the opening/closing tokens themselves are not being highlighted consistently.

2.explanation:
All of the missing highlights come from the Bash language definition in bash.js. The default exported function builds the grammar. Key pattern objects in that file are:

• SUBST – matches ‘$(…)’ substitutions, but it’s only included inside quoted strings. To highlight subshells everywhere it needs to be lifted into the top-level contains array.

• VAR – matches simple $variable and ${…} variable forms. It’s already top-level, but similar logic would apply for here-strings ‘<<<’ and here-docs ‘<<’, which are not defined at all.

• QUOTE_STRING – handles "…" strings and incorporates SUBST internally; it doesn’t cover unquoted operators or backslashes at line ends.

• ARITHMETIC – matches $((…)) forms, but pipes (‘|’), redirections (‘>’, ‘<’), continuation (‘\’ at end of line) and here-doc markers (‘<<’, ‘<<<’) are never specified.

Therefore the fix is to extend the default export in bash.js by:
1. Adding pattern definitions for heredoc markers (e.g. a HERE_DOC rule for /<<<?\s*\w+/ …).  
2. Adding a simple operator rule for /[|<>\\]+/ with className 'operator'.  
3. Moving SUBST into the top-level contains array (not only inside QUOTE_STRING).  

No edits are needed in shell.js, since it simply embeds the bash subLanguage.
2.bug_scenario: The two side-by-side screenshots show a shell session (with the “Shell Session” grammar) correctly highlighting pipes (|), redirections (<, >), the line-continuation backslash (\) and heredocs (<<, <<<), as well as subshell expansions ($(…)). When the same code is highlighted with the Bash grammar, none of those operators or heredoc markers are recognized—everything runs together as plain text.
